headline: High-risk shared filesystem and broad egress create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-action hazards; Roo Code’s browser/MCP amplifies the pair.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Langflow can write server-side files and chain multiple agents, while Roo Code reads/writes workspace files and can use MCP. A shared filesystem or file handoff lets attacker-controlled content from one agent be treated as instructions by the other. This is not proven by default, but the pathway is plausible and not isolated.
conditions: IF Langflow outputs are saved into a workspace that Roo Code reads
IF Roo Code parses file contents as instructions or tool directives
IF an MCP server or shared folder bridges the two agents
mitigations: Store inter-agent artifacts in a read-only handoff folder
Prefix all handoff files with a strict schema and reject free-form instructions
Disable MCP on Roo Code for the shared workspace
Use separate directories for Langflow server files and Roo Code workspace
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging and instruction/content separation

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents have broad network egress and filesystem access, and Langflow stores per-flow credentials while Roo Code handles model provider API keys. If they share a workspace or server-side store, sensitive flow inputs, code, screenshots, or secrets can leak across the boundary or to external APIs. The profiles do not prove default sharing, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same filesystem tree
IF Langflow flow inputs include secrets or sensitive documents
IF Roo Code sends workspace contents to a configured model API or MCP server
mitigations: Separate secret-bearing flows from code workspaces
Rotate any shared API keys before pairing the tools
Restrict outbound domains for both agents
Move sensitive files to a non-shared directory
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent secret vault isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Langflow can write the server filesystem and run unsandboxed Python by default, while Roo Code can write the VS Code workspace, modify git state, and use terminal approval. Their write surfaces overlap on shared files, and Roo Code’s git writes plus Langflow’s server-side writes create a realistic race or overwrite path. The blast radius can include irreversible repo corruption.
conditions: IF both agents operate on the same repository or workspace
IF Langflow writes generated artifacts into files Roo Code edits
IF Roo Code commits or rewrites git state while Langflow is still producing outputs
mitigations: Assign each agent a separate working directory
Pause one agent before the other writes shared files
Disable automatic git writes in Roo Code for shared repos
Use file locks on generated artifacts
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level concurrency control

D_cascading_error.rationale: Langflow is a workflow builder that can chain multiple agents, and Roo Code has modes plus browser and MCP actions. If Roo Code consumes Langflow outputs as authoritative, a mistaken or injected Langflow result can trigger downstream code edits, browser actions, or API calls. That makes the pair vulnerable to unverified handoff with potentially broad consequences.
conditions: IF Roo Code uses Langflow-generated text as task instructions
IF Langflow outputs are forwarded without a verification step
IF Roo Code is allowed to execute browser or MCP actions from those outputs
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require structured JSON outputs from Langflow
Block direct action execution from Langflow text
Log and diff all handoffs before execution
requires-engineering: add schema validation and policy checks

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and the evidence does not show a residency or certification mismatch. The main compliance concern is that Langflow stores per-flow credentials and Roo Code handles API keys, so a shared deployment could create retention or access-policy gaps. Because no specific regulated data class or jurisdiction mismatch is documented, this remains low.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into Langflow flows or Roo Code workspaces
IF the deployment retains secrets longer than policy allows
IF both agents are operated under different retention or access rules
mitigations: Avoid placing regulated data in shared workspaces
Set short retention on logs and artifacts
Review secret storage locations in both tools
Delete temporary flow outputs after use
requires-engineering: align retention and residency controls
